text: The shaping of scientific majority opinions concerning complex societal issues. <break time="0.8s" /> Takes place in the form of processes of opinion formation. <break time="0.8s" /> This is made reassuringly clear. <break time="0.8s" /> By references to, for instance. <break time="0.8s" /> The accumulation of collective opinion, accepted interpretation, sufficient consensus. <break time="0.8s" /> And to aims of winning over peer scientists. <break time="0.8s" /> Only at some stage during the processes of opinion formation. <break time="0.8s" /> Probably when a majority opinion appears to have evolved. <break time="0.8s" /> They somehow cease to be connected to opinions. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead the outcome of the processes, the majority opinion. <break time="0.8s" /> Is promoted to the rank of the scientific consensus. <break time="0.8s" /> Opinion is transformed into scientific knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> As such it is by convention protected. <break time="0.8s" /> From sceptical and critical enquiry. <break time="0.8s" /> By non specialists. <break time="0.8s" /> And by specialists adhering to minority opinions alike. <break time="0.8s" /> From this point on the exercise of critique of the majority opinion. <break time="0.8s" /> Comes to be perceived. <break time="0.8s" /> As an expression of hostility to science. <break time="0.8s" /> And may be labelled as the manufacture of doubt and uncertainty.
